messages.subject: camtrapR v 1.2.3. released
messages.body_plain:
Dear group,
camtrapR version 1.2.3 has been released in CRAN. It expands upon the previous release of version 1.2 and is a major release and improvement compared to version 1.1. Versions 1.2 and 1.2.1 had a few bugs in important functions for which I apologise, all of which should be fixed now.

Here are the key features of the new release:
detectionHistory can create input for multi-season occupancy models
spatialDetectionHistory: improved support for multi-season models
cameraOperation: new argument sessionCol to enable multi-season models
multi-season sample data and updated examples and vignettes
tidyverse support: input tibbles and data.tables accepted instead of data.frames only in all functions
lubridate support: date and date/time formats from lubridate, making it easier to define the dreaded dateFormat / dateTimeFormat arguments (e.g. "ymd" instead of "%Y-%m-%d", "ymd HMS" instead of "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
recordTable: summary statistics for events (e.g. maximum individual count or average temperature within 60 minutes) via 2 new arguments
recordTable: prettier and more concise console output
exifTagNames is more flexible and can return metadata for any user-defined image
changes in package dependencies: ritis, taxize and rgdal are now optional and not required. data.table is a new dependency

For details and the full list of changes please see the package NEWS <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/NEWS>.

Thank you for using camtrapR. If you have any questions, feedback or problems, please let me know.
Kind regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: "lastIndependentRecord" and "lastRecord" difference in "deltaTimeComparedTo" for recordtable
messages.body_plain:
I'm new working with camptrapR and currently trying to figure out the difference between "lastIndependentRecord" and  "lastRecord" diference in deltaTimeComparedTo" in order to create my recordtable. I read the vignettes, the pdf, and other related materials but still not fully understand the difference. I think that and example can help a lot. I know this could be a silly question but it is really important to begin data analysis. Please can someone explain what this means, my attempts to find out through a web search has so far failed.
Kind regards
Camilo
messages.body_snippet: I'm new working with camptrapR and currently trying to figure out the difference between "lastIndependentRecord" and  "lastRecord" diference in deltaTimeComparedTo" in order to create my recordtable.

messages.subject: Re: "lastIndependentRecord" and "lastRecord" difference in "deltaTimeComparedTo" for recordtable
messages.body_plain:
Hi Camilo,
I don't have example data at hand, but imagine this scenario:

A species is detected at a station 3 times in the same day:  1:00pm, 1:30pm, 2:10pm

You run recordTable() with minDeltaTime = 60. The first record (1:00 pm) will always be returned. deltaTimeComparedTo controls how the time differences of the remaining records (record 2 and 3 in this example) are calculated and which of these are returned.

deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastIndependentRecord"
Record 1: is considered an independent record and will be returned
Record 2: time difference to last independent record (record 1) = 30 minutes. Record 2 is therefore not independent and will be omitted (time difference to last independent record < 60 minutes).
Record 3: time difference to last independent record (record 1) = 70 minutes. Record 3 is therefore independent and will be returned (time difference to last independent record > 60 minutes).
> recordTable returns record 1 and 3

deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastRecord"
Record 1: is considered an independent record and will be returned
Record 2: time difference to last record (record 1) = 30 minutes. Record 2 is therefore not independent and will be omitted (time difference to last record < 60 minutes).
Record 3: time difference to last record (record 2) = 40 minutes. Record 3 is therefore not independent and will be omitted (time difference to last record < 60 minutes).
> recordTable returns only record 1

In a more extreme example, imagine records of a species every 10 minutes. minDeltaTime is still 60 minutes.

deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastIndependentRecord" will return the first record and then records every hour.
deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastRecord" will only return the first record, since all subsequent time intervals are less than 60 minutes.

If minDeltaTime = 0, how you set deltaTimeComparedTo doesn't make a difference.

Hope this helps understand how the argument works. If you have further questions, please feel free to ask. I will also add a more in-depth explanation in the vignettes. Thank you for the suggestion.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to set occasion length = a month not # of days?
messages.subject_clean: Is there a way to set occasion length = a month not # of days?
messages.body_plain:
Because months aren't all the same length, and because camtrapR only works with occasion lengths in days, you can't do this as far as I know. If you really wanted to you could collapse the detection histories manually e.g. renaming o1, o2 ... o(n) with dates and collapsing through a pivot table for example; however, your data won't be standardised, either, as you'd have varying numbers of days that make up each detection history block, so you'd probably want standardise the number of days e.g. omitting the 31st day (or, if you're surveying in February, omitting the 29th, 30th, 31st ... unless you're working in a leap year ... ). Long story short, camtrapR only allows occasion lengths in "days", not hours, months, years, so if you want to do this you'll have to do it manually. Weeks simply work better because no matter what time of year, a week always has 7 days, whereas months are just a bit of a pain.

Jarrad

messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to set occasion length = a month not # of days?
messages.subject_clean: Is there a way to set occasion length = a month not # of days?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rachel,
like Jarred said, occasion lengths equal to specific months is currently not implemented in camtrapR. If I find the time I might try to implement this in a coming release. But for now it is not available.

A workaround would be to format date/time in the record table as year-month, create an empty detection history (Station x month) with all 0, then for each station write a 1 into the cells of the detection matrix for every month with a record. I currently don't have any code available for this operation.
This workaround would also not account for varying effort due to the number of days per month (as Jarred pointed out) and also incompletely sampled months (due to setup and retrieval days not on the 1st/last day of the month). As a consequence, your results might be off when effort is not taken into account.

Does anyone else miss this feature? The more interest there is, the sooner I'll address it.
Jürgen
